rejected_rule.statement: A decree in a partition action must be in respect of the land to which the action relates, and if the plaintiff fails to establish their title to that land or the proceedings are not conducted according to the Partition Act, the action must fail.
rejected_rule.supporting_quote: "The course taken by the learned Judge is not authorised by the Act. The plaintiff's proctor has certified under section 12 of the Act that lis pendens has been duly registered... The scheme of the Partition Act is that once an action is instituted and lis pendens is duly registered the action must proceed in respect of the land described in the plaint except where a larger land is made the subject-matter of the action. In such a case the procedure prescribed by section 23 must be followed."
rejected_rule.statute_citation_verbatim: "Section 67, Section 83 (1), and Section 26 (2) (a) of the Partition Act"
